results.note: Verified directly: UncorroboratedDefinition (registry.py:37-42) is a plain optional field on IndicatorDefinition (line 60), default None, no computed/inferred logic. Test (tests/test_uncorroborated.py:31-42) loads an entry with explicit uncorroborated.note and asserts corroboration is None / uncorroborated carries the exact note text.

Verified: test model_dumps a corroborated and an uncorroborated definition and asserts the dicts differ, each carrying the opposite field populated/None (lines 60-68) — real assertions, not vacuous. Caveat carried from prior verdict still applies: this proves distinguishability at the registry-model level only; ingest/corroborate.py (the DB write path) has no reference to `uncorroborated`, so the distinction doesn't yet reach the corroborations table. Story's declared touched files are registry.yaml/registry.py/tests only, so this is in scope.

Verified: load_registry (registry.py:174-188) raises ValueError when has_second_source == is_uncorroborated (both false = silence, both true = double-declare), mirroring reject_wildcards on definable_for (lines 62-69, same file). Test strips the uncorroborated block and asserts ValueError matching 'corroboration declaration'.

Verified: assert_registry_coverage (registry.py:191-215) appends a failure when has_second_source == is_uncorroborated (lines 201-206), extending the existing PRD-002 coverage-checking mechanism. Test constructs a definition with neither field set and asserts AssertionError matching 'corroboration declaration'.

Deterministic gate `uv run python -m ingest.registry --validate` exited 0 (given, and matches the story's DETERMINISTIC GATE RESULTS). Confirmed by reading the shipped registry.yaml directly: its sole entry declares `corroboration` (line 13) and not `uncorroborated`, so has_second_source=True/is_uncorroborated=False are unequal and load_registry's new XOR check does not raise.

note: All five criteria verified by directly reading ingest/registry.py, ingest/registry.yaml, and tests/test_uncorroborated.py (not just trusting the diff or prior verdict). Tests are assertion-bearing and exercise real registry.py logic. One scope caveat carried forward on C2: the `uncorroborated` field is registry/YAML-level only — ingest/corroborate.py, the module that writes actual datapoint/corroboration rows, has zero references to it, so the value/absence distinction is proven at the registry-model level, not the corroborations-table level. This matches the story's declared touched files (registry.yaml/registry.py/tests only) so it does not fail any criterion, but the story's narrative claim that Coin Metrics MVRV itself now ships with this note is not true of the shipped registry.yaml (only btc_daily_close/corroboration is shipped; the MVRV example lives only inside the test file's fixture). No evidence of faked work — tests contain genuine, non-trivial assertions.
